ports.note: Takes a point layer of cases, each with a date, and gives back the clusters it reports as circles: one polygon per cluster, carrying its days, places, observed and expected cases, likelihood ratio and p-value.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no mapping to an external vocabulary. fw:SpaceTimeScan and fw:ScanCluster are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties. The receipt names the date column, the unit, the study period, every record not scanned and why, the limits, the replications, the seed and the random stream, and every cluster reported with its counts and p-value.

changes.description: Day by day, as the outbreak unfolded: a prospective scan each day on the cases known by then, scoring only runs ending that day, with the first day the most likely cluster's p-value was at or under 0.05 and 0.01. Each day's p-value is that day's alone; repeated looks are not corrected for, and the sentence says so. Both modes write a Methods note with the expected count and the log likelihood ratio, instantiated, citing Kulldorff and others 2005 (PLoS Medicine 2(3):e59, verified), which reaches References.

evidence.note: tests/space-time-scan.test.mjs (7 unit checks, the replay and the note among them) and tests/hagelloch-cluster-example.browser.mjs on Chromium, which checks both progress bars, the replay's first flagged day and the reference in References. Lab check 46: the retrospective scan recomputed in numpy; the replay is checked there too (see parity).
